info.title: Referenced Payouts
info.description: The Referenced Payouts API enables partner merchants and developers to process individual referenced payouts to recipients. To use this API, you must request a build notation (BN) code. To learn more or to request a BN code, contact your partner manager or visit the PayPal Partner Portal.

tags.name: referenced-payouts
tags.description: Enables you to create a referenced batch payout and list all items, with details, in a referenced batch payout.

tags.name: referenced-payouts-items
tags.description: Enables you to create a referenced payout item and show details for a payout item, by ID.

tags.name: customer-payouts
tags.description: The Customer Payouts API enables partner merchants and developers to process individual flex payouts to recipients.

post.description: Creates a referenced batch payout for asynchronous, offline processing. Include a `sender_batch_header` object and an `items` array in the request URI.

200.description: An idempotent duplicate request returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code and a JSON response body that lists all items, with details, in the referenced batch payout.

201.description: A successful request returns the HTTP `201 CREATED` status code and a JSON response body that lists all items, with details in case of synchronous processing.

202.description: A successful request returns the HTTP `202 Accepted` status code and a JSON response body that includes a [HATEOAS link](/docs/api/reference/api-responses/#hateoas-links) to the ID for the batch payout.

get.summary: List items in referenced batch payout
get.description: Lists the payout items in a referenced batch payout, by ID. Each item in the list includes payout item details.

200.description: A successful request returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code and a JSON response body that lists all items, with details, in the referenced batch payout.

403.description: Authorization failed due to insufficient permissions.

200.description: If the payout item already exists and was processed, a successful request returns the HTTP `200 OK` status code and a JSON response body that shows payout item details.

201.description: If you omit the `Prefer` request header and the API successfully creates the referenced batch item, a successful request returns the HTTP `201 Created` status code and a JSON response body that shows payout item details.

202.description: If the `Prefer` request header is `respond-async` and the API successfully queued the request for processing, a successful request returns the HTTP `202 Accepted` status code and the API proceeds to process the request asynchronously.

x-enumDescriptions.description: A payout cannot be done for this transaction at this time because the underlying transaction is currently on hold.
The server is already processing a previous request on this reference, please try after some time.
Requested Payout Amount More Than Available Amount.
The application returns this error code when there is no money left to be held in DQ GL which happens when there is no money to be settled to merchants.Ex; PartnerFee >= TxnAmount.
Referenced Transaction Reversal Pending From eCheck.
The reference type is a transaction ID.

referenced_payouts.title: Referenced Payouts
referenced_payouts.description: An array of referenced payout batch items.

payout_directive.description: The payout directive. Defines how the payout is made following the referenced payouts, if required. If you include this directive, all items in the request must be for the same original receiver. Otherwise, the request fails. You can override the payout directive at the item level to a different funding instrument, if required.

item_id.description: The ID for the payout item request.

reference_id.description: The original reference ID, based on `reference_type`, based on the type payout.

payout_transaction_id.description: The encrypted PayPal transaction ID for the payout when the `item_status` is `success`.

disbursement_transaction_id.description: The encrypted PayPal transaction ID for the disbursement when the money is moved from settlement hold to receiver.

external_merchant_id.description: The unique ID for the merchant on the partner side. Can be used to retrieve the PayPal account linked to this ID for the payout.

external_reference_id.description: The reference ID for the request on the partner side. This is an external reference ID and means nothing in PayPal's system. The value is associated with any object created by the call and is included any time the object's data is returned. For example, in webhooks, GET operations, and the POST response.

payee_email.description: The PayPal merchant account email that receives the payout. Can be used to override the default behavior where the payout receiver is derived from the reference that is passed.

payout_amount.description: The amount to be paid to merchant.

payout_destination.description: The encrypted PayPal account number or the ID of the financial instrument that received the payout.

invoice_id.description: The partner invoice ID for this referenced-payouts item. Used for reporting purposes only.

custom.description: The partner custom data for this referenced-payouts item. Used for reporting purposes only.

referenced_payouts_item_list.description: An array of referenced payouts items. For synchronous execution, the maximum number of items is `10`. If you include more than 10 items, the request is processed asynchronously no matter what the partner defined in the `Prefer` request header.

prefer.name: Prefer
prefer.description: Indicates how the client expects the server to process this request. To process the request asynchronously, set this header to `respond-async`. If you omit this header, the API processes the request synchronously.

payouts_batch_id.name: payouts_batch_id
payouts_batch_id.description: The ID of the reference batch payout for which to list items.

payouts_item_id.name: payouts_item_id
payouts_item_id.description: The ID of the referenced payout item for which to show details.
